summary: Quality evidence for ranking small open-weight coding-agent models, as of 2026-11-15. The main public coding-agent leaderboards no longer rank the newest small models. SWE-bench (https://www.swebench.com, data file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SWE-bench/swe-bench.github.io/master/data/leaderboards.json) has no results newer than 2026-02-26, and it dropped the bash-only board on 2026-09-01. The best small rows there are Devstral Small 2512 at 56.4 (mini-SWE-agent, checked) and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B at 51.6 (OpenHands). Terminal-Bench (https://www.tbench.ai/leaderboard) now runs v4.1, and its smallest open entries are GLM-5.3-Flash (321B) at 37.0% and Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (120B-A12B) at 0.3%; no model of 32B or less is listed. BFCL (https://gorilla.cs.berkeley.edu/leaderboard.html, last updated 2026-04-12) and Aider polyglot (last data 2025-10) stop at Qwen3 and gpt-oss. LiveCodeBench's public data stops at 2025-04. Ranking therefore rests on three things: the Artificial Analysis small and medium views (Intelligence Index v5, with many small models scored 0 or missing), LMArena/arena.ai text Elo (updated 2026-11-11), and vendor model cards. NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning card is the most useful single source because it measures Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma 4 26B-A4B, gpt-oss-20b and Nemotron under one harness (https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16). On that and the vendor cards, the strongest models that could run on this machine are Qwen3.8-27B (Aug 2026, dense; vendor reports Terminal-Bench 2.1 73.0 and SWE-bench Pro 61.7), Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Meta Muse Glimmer 30B (vendor SWE-bench Verified 76.0), Gemma 4 31B and 26B-A4B, GLM-4.7-Flash (30B-A3B), Devstral Small 2 (24B), Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B-24GB (2-bit, 22 GB GGUF) and gpt-oss-20b. Vendor scores conflict sharply. Gemma 4 26B-A4B gets SWE-bench Verified 17.4 in Qwen's table and 57.40 in NVIDIA's, and Gemma 4 31B gets 52.0 from Qwen and 66.6 from Meta. Independent results on harder agentic tests are far below vendor claims: Artificial Analysis measured Qwen3.8 27B at only 5.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. For 16 GB of VRAM the hard limit is weight size. In vLLM, only gpt-oss-20b (MXFP4, 13.8 GB of weights, tight), Gemma 4 12B (QAT w4a16, 10.3 GB) and smaller models fit. Every strong 27B to 35B model needs a llama.cpp or Ollama GGUF, either at about 3 to 4 bits (Qwen3.8-27B UD-IQ4_XS is 14.35 GB, UD-Q3_K_XL is 13.15 GB) or with MoE experts offloaded to system RAM. Ollama's OpenCode integration doc says OpenCode needs a context window of at least 64k (https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/opencode). OpenCode's providers doc says vLLM models it discovers start with tools disabled (https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/).

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B
models.architecture: dense hybrid attention (linear attention on 48 of 64 layers), vision tower, built-in MTP head
official_quantized: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF: UD-IQ4_XS 14.35 GB, UD-Q3_K_XL 13.15 GB, UD-Q4_K_XL 17.66 GB
models.vllm: recipe https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B: vLLM 0.17.0+, image vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38, --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3. On a single 32 GB RTX 5090, NVFP4 needs --enforce-eager and --max-model-len 32768.
models.llamacpp_ollama: Unsloth: 4-bit quants run on 16-19 GB VRAM such as an RTX 5080; Ollama qwen3.8 has tools, thinking and vision tags
models.fit_16gb: vLLM does not fit (NVFP4 is about 21 GB). llama.cpp: UD-IQ4_XS 14.35 GB or UD-Q3_K_XL 13.15 GB fits in VRAM with modest KV (only 16 of 64 layers keep a KV cache); Q4_K_M at 18 GB needs partial offload.
models.coding_agent_evidence: Vendor self-reported: Terminal Bench 2.1 (Terminus) 73.0, SWE-bench Pro 61.7, LiveCodeBench v6 90.3 (Claude Code harness). Independent: Artificial Analysis Terminal-Bench 4.0 is 5.6% at Xhigh and Intelligence Index v5 is 20.1 (best small model except Nanbeige4.3-33B). arena.ai text Elo 1434.
models.notes: Thinking is on by default, and preserve_thinking is on by default. Sampling settings: thinking mode temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20; non-thinking mode temp 0.7, top_p 0.8, presence_penalty 1.5.

Meta reports SWE-Bench Verified 76.0, SWE-Bench Pro 51.2 and TerminalBench 2.1 51.7 for a 30B dense Apache-2.0 model released Aug 2026, vs Qwen3.6-27B at 77.2 / 50.2 / 60.7

Vendor: SWE-bench Verified 68.0%, Multilingual 55.7%, Terminal Bench 2 22.5%
Google card gives no SWE-bench numbers. LiveCodeBench v6 / Tau2: 31B 80.0/76.9, 26B A4B 77.1/68.2, 12B 72.0/69.0. Context is 256K for 12B and up, 128K for E2B/E4B.
Unsloth: 'Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit quants work on 16-19GB VRAM like RTX 5080'. Recommended UD-Q4_K_XL is 17.66 GB, so 16 GB VRAM means partial offload or UD-IQ4_XS at 14.35 GB.
vLLM recipe: on one RTX 5090 (32 GB), Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 starts only with --enforce-eager and --max-model-len 32768. On 2x RTX 5090, NVFP4 weights are 10.6-12.0 GiB per GPU, about 21-24 GiB in total.

No 27B+ model has a vendor checkpoint that fits in 16 GB VRAM under vLLM: Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 21.9 GB, Gemma-4-31B w4a16 23.3 GB, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 37.5 GB, Lightning NVFP4 21.6 GB. gpt-oss-20b at 13.76 GB and Gemma-4-12B w4a16 at 10.26 GB do fit.
Ollama docs: 'OpenCode requires a context length of 64k or higher'
OpenCode providers doc: vLLM models it discovers 'start with tools disabled'; default local endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1

NVIDIA's Aug 11 2026 local-AI posts name no GPU or VRAM-specific model picks. They cite Qwen3.8-27B at 131 tok/s on an RTX 5090 with MTP (llama.cpp Q4_K_M) and list llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and Unsloth as runtimes.

Ollama tags: qwen3.8:27b 18GB/256K; qwen3.6:27b-q4_K_M 17GB; gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat 16GB; gemma4:12b-it-qat 7.2GB; gpt-oss:20b 14GB/128K; devstral-small-2:24b 15GB/384K; glm-4.7-flash 19GB/198K; qwen3-coder-next 52GB

DeepSeek released no small models in the last 12 months. DeepSeek-V4-Flash has about 291B params and V4.1-Flash-1017 about 763B (HF safetensors totals); the only small option is the older R1-0528-Qwen3-8B distill (2025-05-29).

gaps: No independent coding-agent leaderboard covers the current small models (Qwen3.6/3.8, Gemma 4, Nemotron 3.5, Muse Glimmer). The SWE-bench board stops at 2026-02-26 and dropped bash-only, Terminal-Bench 4.1 lists no model of 32B or less, BFCL has no rows after Qwen3, and Aider and LiveCodeBench are stale. The ranking leans on vendor cards.
No tau2-bench official leaderboard was checked (no URL found in time); tau2 values come from Artificial Analysis and the vendor cards.
LMArena/arena.ai rows come from a single WebFetch summary; Cloudflare blocked a raw read. The webdev board was not read.
Artificial Analysis Coding and Agentic index values were not in the page data (null). Intelligence Index v5 reads 0 for several small models, which likely means not yet computed.
Gemma 4 vLLM tool-call and reasoning parser names were not confirmed: the vLLM recipe JSON for google/gemma-4-* returned a Next.js error page and the HF card does not give them.
Muse Glimmer vLLM support and parser names were not checked; its card mentions only llama.cpp for RTX.
Qwen3-Coder-Next SWE-bench numbers appear only as an image in the card; not extracted.
No official NVIDIA, Ollama or OpenCode page names a recommended model for 16 GB GPUs; such lists exist only in third-party blogs (not used).
Real throughput and KV-cache capacity on an 80-175 W RTX 5080 Laptop with 16 GB were not measured; fit estimates come from file sizes only.
Nanbeige4.3-33B (top of the AA small view) and K2 Horizon models were not evaluated for tool calling or license.
